name: What happens if my rear addition was built without a permit?

mainEntity.name: Can I legalize an existing rear addition that was built without a permit, and what usually happens during the process?
mainEntity.text: Can I legalize an existing rear addition that was built without a permit, and what usually happens during the process?

acceptedAnswer.text: An unpermitted rear addition is common in older Los Angeles-area homes, but legalizing it can be more involved than permitting a new project. The existing work must usually be documented, inspected, and compared against current code requirements. If the structure is hidden behind finished walls or lacks clear records, inspectors may require openings or additional engineering to verify framing, foundation, electrical, plumbing, and safety conditions. Some older additions also need upgrades because today’s codes are stricter than when the work was originally done. If the goal is to sell, refinance, or remodel the home, it is usually better to address the issue early rather than wait for a problem during escrow or construction. The process is often easier when the homeowner can produce drawings, photos, or prior records. A permit professional should first determine whether legalization is practical before any cosmetic work is started.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, an unpermitted rear addition can often be legalized, but it usually must be brought up to current code. That may require opening walls, structural verification, new engineering, and corrections before approval can be issued.
